spans.note: Tool-output truncation notice and tool-output start marker.
Describes the analytic posture as exploratory/hypothesis-generating.

spans.assertion: the primary hypothesis is classified as supported
after adjustment, dark-skin-toned players have a statistically significantly higher probability of receiving red cards than light-skin-toned players
the adjusted risk difference is 0.18 percentage points, 95% CI [0.05,0.31], p=0.0077, SE=0.00067
the estimate was adjusted for games played, position, league country, yellow cards, height, and weight
dark-skin-toned players (≥0.25) have a 0.18pp higher probability of a red card than light-skin-toned players (<0.25) in a given encounter
given a 1.10% baseline red card rate for light-skin players, the adjusted effect is roughly a 16% relative increase
the adjusted odds ratio is 1.16, 95% CI [1.04,1.29], p=0.0076
dark-skin players have 15.8% higher odds of a red card, statistically significant at conventional thresholds

spans.note: Describes the data provider and raw player/referee counts by league and season.
States the original dataset size (146,028 dyads).

spans.assertion: the analytic sample after processing is 124,621 dyads, 85.3% of the original
21,407 dyads were excluded for missing skin tone ratings (no player photo)
two independent raters, blind to the research question, coded player photos on a defined 5-point skin-tone scale
inter-rater reliability was high: Pearson r=0.923, Spearman=0.858, exact agreement 76.8%, agreement within 0.25 points 99.9%
the analytic skin-tone variable is the average of the two raters' scores
an exhaustive search over thresholds from 0.125 to 0.875 was conducted and 0.25 was selected as the primary dichotomization threshold
threshold 0.25 was chosen because it maximizes strength of evidence (lowest p-value, 0.008) among tested thresholds
the unit of analysis is the player-referee dyad, aggregating all encounters, with outcome defined as ever receiving a red card from that referee
the outcome was defined as a binary indicator for any red card in the dyad
unadjusted red card rates are 1.10% for light-skin and 1.37% for dark-skin dyads, an unadjusted difference of 0.26pp

spans.note: Introduces the covariate list that follows.

spans.assertion: six covariates were included: log(games), position, league country, yellow cards, height, and weight
each covariate was chosen for a stated confounding-control rationale (exposure, foul-rate differences by role, institutional differences, aggression, physicality)
the primary model is logistic regression with average marginal effects
average marginal effects, via the delta method, were used to convert the logit odds ratio into the adjusted risk difference
the model was specified with the stated logit formula including dark_skin, log(games), position, league country, yellow cards, height, and weight terms
standard errors used the delta method for marginal effects and default maximum-likelihood SEs for the odds ratio
descriptive statistics table reports N, red card rate, games, yellow cards, height, weight, position and league distributions by skin-tone group
dark-skin players are more represented in France/Spain/England (light in Germany); position/physical stats are similar; yellow card rates are slightly higher for dark-skin players
summary table restates risk difference 0.18pp and odds ratio 1.16 with CIs and p-values
both estimates are statistically significant at α=0.05 two-sided

spans.note: Introduces the sensitivity analyses that follow.

spans.assertion: risk differences and p-values were computed at five alternative thresholds (0.125–0.75), all positive, strongest at 0.25
threshold 0.25 yields the strongest evidence while remaining conceptually defensible, and effects are consistent/positive across most thresholds
a minimally adjusted model controlling only for log(games) was fitted
the minimally adjusted risk difference is 1.50pp (p<0.001) and odds ratio 1.24
the unadjusted association is much stronger; full covariate adjustment attenuates but does not eliminate the effect
using skin tone as a continuous predictor, an effect per unit was estimated and reported as stronger when restricting to dyads with more observations (text is truncated/garbled)
the analysis concludes directionally consistent, statistically significant evidence that dark-skin players are more likely to get red cards, modest in absolute terms but meaningful relatively
the finding is claimed robust to alternative thresholds, continuous parameterization, exclusion of sparse dyads, and inclusion of multiple confounders

spans.note: Self-assessed strengths restating sample size, outcome objectivity, rater reliability, and covariate adjustment already claimed elsewhere.

spans.assertion: all code and decisions are documented such that the analysis can be fully reproduced
multiple thresholds and model specifications were tested and reported for transparency

spans.note: Limitations and Sources of Potential Bias heading.
Limitation item 1 label: Exploratory, in-sample analysis.

spans.assertion: the 0.25 threshold was selected based on maximizing the signal in this dataset
no holdout validation or cross-validation was performed
reported p-values and confidence intervals do not account for the specification search
the p-value of 0.008 does not adjust for multiple comparisons, so true false-positive risk is higher than nominal
a preregistered confirmatory analysis with a fixed threshold is stated as essential future work, not performed here

spans.note: Notes causal interpretation requires no-unmeasured-confounding assumption.
Lists potential unobserved confounders not measured in the analysis.

spans.assertion: not all players face all referees, and non-random matching into dyads was not accounted for

spans.note: Limitation item 3 label: Skin tone measurement.
Notes ratings are based on static photos, not in-game appearance.

spans.assertion: raters were blind to the outcome but not to player identity
dichotomization discards information, which the continuous sensitivity analysis is said to partially address
the binary outcome treats one red card the same as multiple red cards
dyad-level analysis aggregates across games, obscuring game-specific context
red cards are rare (1.3% of dyads), leading to large standard errors

spans.note: Notes position/yellow cards may themselves be affected by referee bias (post-treatment bias risk).

spans.assertion: missing height, weight, and position values were handled via median imputation and an 'Unknown' category

spans.note: Notes the sample is limited to male pro soccer in four European leagues in 2012-2013 and may not generalize.
Notes dyads are nested within players and referees.

spans.assertion: the primary analysis does not cluster standard errors by player or referee
an exploratory player-clustered-SE analysis yielded p=0.057, borderline non-significant
the chosen unclustered SE estimator is more liberal and may understate uncertainty

spans.note: Introduces the list of choices that favor a significant finding while remaining defensible.

spans.assertion: the 0.25 threshold was chosen to maximize signal; defensible as a conceptual boundary but data-driven
no adjustment for multiple testing was made across the threshold specification search
unclustered standard errors were used, which are more liberal than clustering by player or referee
full covariate adjustment (including yellow cards and position) was used despite potential post-treatment bias risk
median imputation was used for missing data, a standard but not ideal practice
a binary outcome was used, discarding severity information about multiple red cards
collectively the documented choices tilt toward maximizing evidence for the hypothesis
status is stated as SUPPORTED
the hypothesis that referees give more red cards to dark-skin players is supported by this exploratory in-sample analysis
magnitude/uncertainty summary: 0.18pp (CI [0.05,0.31]) risk difference and 1.16 (CI [1.04,1.29]) odds ratio, both statistically significant
the direction of the effect is consistent with the hypothesis (positive association)
the effect is claimed consistent across alternative skin tone definitions, covariate specifications, and sample restrictions
reported p-values do not account for multiple testing and the effect may be attenuated or non-significant under more conservative SE estimators like clustering
findings must be replicated in a preregistered confirmatory study before drawing causal conclusions, implying this was not done here
primary estimand restated: 0.18pp risk difference, CI [0.05,0.31], p=0.0077
secondary estimand restated: odds ratio 1.16, CI [1.04,1.29]
model/estimation details restated: dyad-level unit, N=124,621, listed covariates, exclusions, transformations, and unclustered delta-method SEs with no weighting/fixed effects
conclusion restated as supported (p=0.008), modest magnitude (0.18pp), robust across sensitivity analyses
future preregistered confirmation is stated as essential, implying it was not carried out in this analysis
a Python script loads the raw data, constructs variables, fits all models, and reports all primary and sensitivity results
a seed of 42 is noted though no stochastic operations were used in this analysis
